question: Which exact 3.101.043 globals and wrappers carry the core adapter, cpevent registration, L2CAP owner, L2CAP requests, and stock pair-request forwarding?
prototype_hypothesis: 0x2013DBE4 stores the core adapter instance, 0x2013DBE0 stores the cpevent registration handle, and 0x2013BDBC stores the L2CAP FSM owner. sub_C805B0C, sub_C805B38, and sub_C805BE8 enqueue connect, disconnect, and CID-submit requests; sub_C709E90 forwards the stock pair request through the adapter reply wrapper.
callsite_evidence: sub_CA40ED4 creates the core Bluetooth adapter and stores the returned object in dword_2013DBE4; sub_CA40F68 directly returns dword_2013DBE4.
sub_CA40E3C registers cpevent through sub_CAA5048 when adapter state becomes ON and stores the returned handle in dword_2013DBE0; on OFF it passes that handle to sub_CAA5108 and clears the global.
sub_C805B0C, sub_C805B38, and sub_C805BE8 all load dword_2013BDBC and submit their incoming request data with distinct handlers through the same owner queue helper sub_C7EB988.
sub_C709E90 contains gap_pair_request_callback and forwards the stock request to sub_C3B0050 with the live adapter context and device address.
control_flow_evidence: The globals have distinct writers and consumer families: 0x2013DBE4 is an adapter object, 0x2013DBE0 is a registration token, and 0x2013BDBC is an FSM owner root. None is interchangeable with a callback table or callable address.
The three L2CAP wrappers preserve their request arguments before loading the same owner and selecting different owner-local work handlers, confirming both address family and queue-only behavior.
ownership_analysis: The three globals and their pointed objects are firmware-owned and borrowed. Connect/disconnect/CID request ownership follows each stock queue wrapper: callers must keep or transfer request/buffer storage exactly as required by the target-private interface and active owner lifecycle.
unsafe_assumptions: The cpevent registration handle is not an adapter pointer and must only be used by the matching event registration lifecycle.
Exact static control flow establishes globals and wrappers; production module use on a physical 3.101.043 target remains unprobed.
recommended_probe: On exact 3.101.043, observe adapter ON/OFF transitions and cpevent registration, then establish and tear down one L2CAP channel while validating owner stability, CID submission, and pair-request forwarding.

artifacts.role: core adapter creation and global writer
